description: WeatherShift, a joint project of Arup and Argos Analytics, adjusts building simulation weather files for future climate. Its Heat tool uses CMIP6 climate model data to produce future typical-year EPW files (fTMY) and future ASHRAE design day files (fDD) for several future periods. Users view free month-by-month projected changes in temperature, heat index, humidity, dew point, solar radiation and wind for pre-loaded public domain U.S. Department of Energy EPW locations, under RCP 4.5 or RCP 8.5 and warming percentiles from 10% to 95%; other sites need an uploaded EPW or design day file as the basis. A companion Rain tool covers future rainfall, and the site also has a library page. Coverage: any location with a base weather file. Access: free viewing; files cost US$285 for the first scenario and US$200 for each additional one. Licence: commercial. Caveats: the page describes RCP scenarios while citing CMIP6 data, and projections carry model uncertainty. Simulation uses: stress-testing building energy, cooling and drainage designs against future heat and rainfall. Related records: CIBSE weather data, Meteonorm Climate and the ORNL future typical meteorological years.
